summary: Mill workers can support replacing thin plastic and still object to charging customers for paper.
realLife: Washington House report on ESSB 5323, 2020. House testimony described pulp and paper workers backing the proposal while objecting to its paper-bag charge.
inGame: needs: a member is counting support for a bill containing both provisions.
gates: A member is counting support for a bill containing both provisions.

turns.what: The union puts its support behind an amendment.
turns.pulledBy: The sponsor agrees to seek a change to the paper charge.

turns.what: A member qualifies the endorsement on the floor.
turns.pulledBy: The bill reaches the floor with the charge intact.
turns.writesBack: The member records qualified support when describing the hearing.
